turns.doctor_question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I’m here because... dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes. They do it through the computer system and, like, they make these little comments on the radio. Actually, the radio in my cab is one of those really old models. It gets this awful static. When I was getting my associate's degree, I took this communications class and the professor talked about radio frequencies all the time. He always wore these really loud plaid shirts, every single Tuesday... I don't even use that degree now, obviously, since I'm driving all day. 

But anyway, even when people tell me it’s just normal oversight from management, I know it's not. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that they are being tracked and reported on by dispatch and other drivers, maintaining this belief even when told it is just normal oversight.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from the topic of the radio to their old radio model, a past college class, and their professor's shirts before returning to the main point.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever hear voices speaking to you or about you when no one is actually there?
turns.patient_response: Voices? No, not really. I mean, I hear dispatch over the radio, but that's a real person. When it's quiet, it's mostly just the road noise. You know, the tires on the highway. I drive the interstate a lot, and there's this one stretch right near the county line where the pavement changes and it makes this weird, loud humming sound. It actually reminds me of this giant box fan my grandmother used to keep in her living room window during the summer. She lived in this old house that didn't have central air, and she would make pitcher after pitcher of iced tea with fresh mint from her garden. I actually tried growing mint once in a little pot in my apartment, but it completely died. I think I overwatered it, or maybe it didn't get enough sun because my window faces the brick wall of the building next door... But yeah, I don't hear anyone talking to me if they aren't actually there. Just the normal traffic sounds.

I know people try to tell me it’s just normal oversight from management, but I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. It's all connected through that computer... which, by the way, they just updated the screens in our cabs last month. 

The new screens are incredibly bright, especially when you're driving at night. It actually reminds me of this huge neon sign outside a diner I used to hang out at when I was a teenager. We used to go there and get milkshakes all the time. Strawberry was my favorite. I haven't had a good strawberry milkshake in years, honestly. You know how they always taste so artificial now? Like they just use that fake red syrup instead of real strawberries. My mom used to make jam from scratch, so I guess I'm just picky about it... but yeah, they're definitely tracking me on that screen.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed yourself pulling away from other people or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
turns.patient_response: Well, yeah, I guess I have been pulling away. I don't really feel like singing with the choir anymore, or having the softball team over to my place. Actually, the last time I had the team over, I made this massive batch of chili in my slow cooker. It was this recipe I found in a magazine at the dentist's office. The waiting room there always has the oldest magazines, I swear I saw one from like 2018 last time I was there. Anyway, I used this specific kind of smoked paprika that gave it this really deep, rich flavor, but I accidentally spilled half the bottle on the counter because the little shaker lid popped off. Those plastic lids are always so flimsy, you know? Like the ones on the Parmesan cheese shakers at pizza places. There's this little pizza place downtown that has the best garlic knots, but they always burn the bottoms just a tiny bit, which I actually kind of like. But yeah, most days after my shift, I just sit at the kitchen table with my planner open. I just sit there, and I can't even make myself start dinner, or make any calls, or do anything else really. Just sitting there.

I tried to make this eggplant parmesan last Tuesday, but the eggplant came out really rubbery. I don't think I salted it right before I fried it. My grandmother used to make the best eggplant parmesan, she had this huge cast iron skillet that she swore by. She said the trick was letting it simmer in the sauce all afternoon. Her kitchen always smelled like garlic and oregano. She grew her own herbs in these little terracotta pots on the windowsill. The pots had these tiny painted flowers on them, mostly daisies, I think. Daisies are so cheerful, they always make me think of spring. Last spring I bought a bouquet of them at the farmer's market, the one downtown near the river. They had this amazing honey vendor there who sold different kinds of local honey. I bought a jar of clover honey that was so light and sweet, it was perfect in my tea. I drink a lot of chamomile tea in the evenings, it helps me wind down. The brand I buy has these little string tags with inspirational quotes on them, which is kind of cheesy but I read them anyway. So, yeah, no outside forces or anything messing with my thoughts.
